reassignedInterfaces._note: Ids the 910 engine addresses that DO exist in the 950 cache but hold different content there. invention_910._note: RE-DERIVED FOR 950, NOT RE-PINNED. The 910 engine means the Invention interface by 1530 (InventionManager opens it as setInterface(false, 1708, 71, 1530) and ButtonHandler/PacketRepository branch on it). 947 had no group 3/1530 at all, so the 947 table listed it absent. The 950 cache DOES have 3/1530, but it is not that interface: it holds 7 components whose text is 'WWWWWWWWWWWW has invited you to join the neighbourhood:' with Accept (file 3) and Decline (file 6) buttons -- a neighbourhood invite popup, one of 14 index-3 groups new in 950 (292, 486, 518, 908, 1143, 1499, 1511, 1512, 1514, 1516, 1518, 1530, 1534, 1538; none were dropped). So the absent flag is not merely stale: the id is now occupied by unrelated content, which is exactly the case the flag existed to prevent, and a 910 Invention emitter reaching it would open an invite popup. Blocked in both resolvers.

_varsNote: Every varbit declares the base varp and bit range the 950 cache decodes for it (2/69), so a re-dumped cache that moves a varbit onto a different varp rejects the table instead of silently rewriting the wrong bits. That check earned its keep on the 947->950 port: it caught hitpoints. All eleven varbits below were re-decoded from 950RevTest/cache 2/69 on 2026-09-10 and, beyond the decode, cross-checked by scanning index 12 of both caches for the scripts that read each id and comparing the two sets. Scan coverage, stated plainly because it is not total: the 950 opcode numbers were derived by aligning the 19,883 script pairs that recompiled instruction-for-instruction out of the 20,551 groups the two caches share, and with that map 20,988 of the 950 cache's 21,098 groups and 20,477 of the 947 cache's 20,577 decode; the ~0.5 percent that do not were not searched. Ten varbits decode to the identical base varp and bit range on both caches AND have the same reader scripts (interface_mode 27169 and legacy_combat_mode 27168 picked up 3 and 2 additional readers, which is content growth, not a move). The eleventh, hitpoints, moved and is now a varp -- see its note. The varps below are only proved to EXIST by the loader (2/60 has no width or meaning to check), so each was additionally cross-checked the same way: varp 462, 463, 679 and 8971 have byte-identical reader-script sets on the 947 and 950 caches.
